locator.section: 8.4 Reaction initiation at radical or charge sites (gamma-H rearrangement of EE+ ions, Kraft and Spiteller 1967, arrow labelled 'rH')

evidence.curator_note: gamma-D rearrangement (arrow 'rH') of an even-electron (EE+) ion, a deuterium-labelling scheme (Kraft and Spiteller 1967) that the text calls a 'gamma-H rearrangement to an unsaturated group with beta-cleavage' closely similar to the OE+. Equations 4.33/4.35/4.36. Because the ion is CLOSED-SHELL, all arrows are double-barbed (2-electron), NOT the three-fishhook radical push of the OE+. analogues. The migrating atom is a DEUTERIUM (real experimental label), written [2H] and atom-mapped (map 15) so its C-D bond can be referenced; a second, spectator D (map 16) sits on the same gamma-carbon (the book draws the gamma-carbon as a -CD2- with one D up-right, one D down-left). The unsaturated group receiving the D is the exocyclic methylene C(=CH2) (map 2 = map 3). Through the drawn six-membered ring the gamma-D (map 15) transfers to the methylene carbon (map 3, becoming the -CH2D / 'DCH2' of the product), the C2=C3 methylene pi bond shifts to the C1-C2 bond (forming the (HO)2C=C enol double bond), and the charge relays from the dihydroxycarbenium carbon (map 1) to the gamma-carbon (map 6, now a +). ARC COUNT: Book draws 2 arc(s) on the precursor - the large sweeping arc from the gamma-D to the CH2 methylene (move <1>, the C-D bonding pair migrating as a hydride, bond 6-15 -> bond 3-15) and the small arc at the methylene/'+' carbon (move <2>, the C2=C3 pi pair -> the C1-C2 bond). Both drawn arcs are encoded; no implicit hook is needed (closed-shell 2-electron process). LOCALIZATION (convention C): the cation is a delocalized allyl/oxocarbenium; the precursor is written in the single localized form with the '+' on the dihydroxycarbenium carbon (map 1, protonated-carboxyl / carboxylic-acid-enol cation) and a genuine C(=CH2) methylene at map 2 - the form these arrows consume. The book draws the resonance partner (formal '+' on the central carbon, C=C to the C(OH)2). INSTANTIATION: the chain length (n-propyl terminus, two CH2 between the gamma-CD2 and the methylene) is transcribed as drawn; the parent is a 2-substituted acrylic-acid EE+ fragment, C9H15D2O2+, m/z 159.135 (curator-computed, no m/z printed on the page).

locator.section: 8.4 Reaction initiation at radical or charge sites (beta-cleavage of the rearranged EE+ ion, arrow labelled 'i')

evidence.curator_note: beta-cleavage (arrow 'i') of the rearranged carbocation. The '+' now sits on the former gamma-carbon (map 6); beta-scission cleaves the Calpha-Cbeta bond (map4-map5) and forms the Cbeta=Cgamma double bond (map5-map6), expelling the neutral alkene CH2=C(D)-CH2CH2CH3 (2-deuterio-1-pentene, C5H9D, keeping the spectator D map 16) and leaving the charge on the allyl/oxocarbenium fragment (map 4 now a primary cation). ARC COUNT: Book draws 1 arc(s) - the single curved arrow on the intermediate running from the Calpha-Cbeta bond up to the '+' on the gamma-carbon; it is the one double-barbed (2-electron) move encoded here. The cleaved Calpha-Cbeta bond IS incident to Cbeta, one of the two atoms of the new Cbeta=Cgamma pi bond - correct beta-scission geometry. DELOCALIZATION (convention C): the product cation is the delocalized allyl/oxocarbenium [CH2-C(CH2D)-C(OH)2]+; it is written in the single localized form these arrows produce, with the '+' on the terminal CH2 (map 4) and the C(OH)2=C enol double bond (map1=map2) retained. The book draws the resonance partner (CH2=C, '+' delocalized onto the C(OH)2). The product m/z 88.050 (C4H6DO2+) is curator-computed (no m/z printed on the page).

NO MOD rule is assigned to Equation 8.35 (rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no 8.35 entry). Cross-link checked, not asserted: the closely-related rules IMS_4_35_rHalpha ('[C]1[C]2([H]3)[C]4[C]5[C]6{=}[N+.]8...>>...[C.]5[C]6{=}[N+]8([H]3)...') and IMS_4_33_rH/alpha_1/alpha_2 encode the ODD-ELECTRON (OE+., note the [N+.]/radical products and the three-fishhook H-migration) gamma-H rearrangement with beta-cleavage. Equation 8.35 is the EVEN-ELECTRON (EE+) counterpart: closed-shell throughout, two-electron arrows, no radical anywhere - so those OE+. rules do NOT match this substrate's electron count and would not fire on it. The text itself flags this scheme as only 'closely similar' to Eqs 4.33/4.35/4.36 and notes the incidence with EE+ ions is much lower than with OE+. ions (Zollinger and Seibl 1985). MS context: an EE+ fragment ion (not the [M]+. molecular ion), studied via metastable/EE+ rearrangement; adduct null. All m/z here (precursor 159.135, product 88.050, ethylene-analogue neutral 71.084) are curator-computed from the transcribed instantiation because the page prints no m/z or intensity (it is a D-labelling mechanism scheme).
